title: Crime
about: Collocations for talking about crime: kinds of criminals and what happens to them in court and in prison, and the phrases politicians and newspapers use about crime, such as petty crime, a spate of burglaries and tackle crime.

parts.title: Common mistakes
parts.note: Steal — про річ, яку взяли: steal a car / some money. Rob — про людину або установу, яку пограбували: rob an old man / a bank; що саме забрали — rob sb of sth. Steal часто вживають у пасиві: My bag was stolen. «У мене вкрали гаманець» — My wallet was stolen або I had my wallet stolen. Burgle — обікрасти будинок чи квартиру: Our flat was burgled. У таблиці — ще кілька типових пасток цього юніту.

rows: My bike was stolen. / I had my bike stolen.
I was stolen in the street
I was robbed in the street.

items.pattern: a hardened criminal / offender · adjective + noun
items.meaning: someone who has committed a lot of crimes and is not likely to change
items.example: My grandmother still can't believe that the polite young man next door was a **hardened criminal**.
more: Social workers try to stop young shoplifters from becoming **hardened criminals**.
Even **hardened criminals** sometimes change when someone gives them a real chance.
items.watchOut: «Закоренілий злочинець» — a hardened criminal (від harden — загартувати, зробити твердим). Не rooted criminal (калька з «корінь») і зазвичай не hard criminal.

items.pattern: commit a crime / an offence / a serious offence · commit – committed – committed
items.meaning: do something that is against the law
items.example: If you use your phone while you're driving, you **commit an offence**, even when you've stopped at traffic lights.
more: The man told the court he had **committed the crime** because he needed money for his family.
Selling cigarettes to children is a **serious offence**, and the shop could lose its licence.
items.watchOut: «Скоїти злочин» — commit a crime / an offence, не make a crime. У розмові почуєш і do a crime, але стандартно — commit. Offence тут — правопорушення; у значенні «образа» воно живе в інших висловах (take offence — образитися). Британське написання — offence, американське — offense.

items.pattern: serve a sentence (of ten years) · serve two years / serve time (in prison)
items.meaning: spend a period of time in prison, or doing another punishment, after a court has decided it
items.example: Her brother is **serving a sentence** for fraud and writes to the family every week.
more: The shoplifter didn't go to prison: she **served her sentence** in the community, cleaning parks.
He **served time** in prison as a young man and now talks to schools about it.
items.watchOut: «Відбувати покарання, відсидіти» — serve a sentence / serve time, не sit a sentence і не sit three years (калька з «відсидіти три роки»). Pass a sentence робить суддя: виносить вирок.

items.pattern: a convicted criminal / thief / fraudster · be convicted of sth
items.meaning: someone who a court of law has officially decided is guilty of a crime
items.example: Some charities help **convicted criminals** find work when they leave prison.
more: She was **convicted of** shoplifting at nineteen and has regretted it ever since.
The man who sold us the fake concert tickets turned out to be a **convicted fraudster**.
items.watchOut: «Засуджений» (суд визнав винним) — convicted, найчастіше з of: convicted of theft, не convicted in theft. Condemned — засуджений морально або до смертної кари.

items.pattern: have a (previous) conviction for robbery / theft / drink-driving
items.meaning: have been found guilty of a particular crime by a court in the past
items.example: The driver already **had a conviction for drink-driving**, so this time he was banned for three years.
more: You must tell the employer if you **have a conviction for** theft.
Her **conviction for** fraud was a shock to everyone at the tennis club.
items.watchOut: Conviction має ще значення «переконання» (strong convictions). «Судимість за…» — a conviction for…, з прийменником for.

items.pattern: a political prisoner · release / free political prisoners
items.meaning: someone kept in prison because of their political beliefs or actions, not for an ordinary crime
items.example: Her grandfather spent eight years as a **political prisoner** because he wrote articles against the government.
more: Thousands of people marched through the capital to demand the release of all **political prisoners**.
The museum in the old prison tells the stories of the **political prisoners** who were kept there.

items.pattern: a common criminal / thief · negative
items.meaning: an ordinary criminal with no special reason or ideals; said with disapproval
items.example: He calls himself a businessman, but the newspapers call him a **common criminal**.
more: The film shows the famous robber as a hero, but in real life he was just a **common criminal**.
Her lawyer argued that she was a desperate mother, not a **common criminal**.
items.watchOut: Common тут — не «спільний», а «звичайний, простий», зі зневагою: a common criminal, a common thief. Порівняй: a political prisoner сидить за погляди.

items.pattern: an act of terrorism / violence / vandalism · commit an act of terrorism
items.meaning: an attack carried out to frighten people for political reasons
items.example: Police quickly said the fire at the station was an accident, not an **act of terrorism**.
more: Several **acts of terrorism** in the 1970s changed the way airports check passengers' bags.
Most countries treat hijacking a plane as an **act of terrorism**.
items.watchOut: «Теракт» — an act of terrorism або a terrorist attack; terror act звучить як калька. Act of + іменник працює й з іншими словами: an act of vandalism, an act of kindness.

items.pattern: have a criminal record · have no criminal record / a clean record
items.meaning: an official list kept by the police of the crimes someone has been found guilty of
items.example: One silly mistake at nineteen left him with a **criminal record**.
more: Some countries won't give you a visa if you have a **criminal record**.
She was relieved to hear that a parking fine doesn't give you a **criminal record**.
items.watchOut: «Мати судимість» — have a criminal record (або have a conviction); «несудимий» — has no criminal record / has a clean record. Record тут — запис, а не «рекорд».

items.pattern: a young / juvenile offender · a prison / institution for young offenders
items.meaning: a person under eighteen who has broken the law
items.example: The project gives **young offenders** the chance to learn a trade instead of going back to crime.
more: The court for **juvenile offenders** is less formal than an adult court.
Many **young offenders** say they started stealing because they were bored.
items.watchOut: Offender — правопорушник, від offence. Це не той, хто когось образив: образити — offend, але offender майже завжди про закон. Juvenile читається /ˈdʒuːvənaɪl/.

items.pattern: the fight against crime / drugs · (help / join) in the fight against crime
items.meaning: everything the police, the government and ordinary people do to reduce crime
items.example: Neighbourhood watch groups play a big part in **the fight against crime** in our area.
more: Volunteers who patrol the park at night are doing their bit in **the fight against crime**.
Our head teacher believes that **the fight against crime** starts in the classroom.
items.watchOut: «Боротьба з» — the fight against, не the fight with (fight with sb — битися з кимось). «Злочинність» — просто crime, а не criminality.

items.pattern: target serious / street / vehicle crime · target burglars / pickpockets
items.meaning: make a particular kind of crime or criminal the main focus of police work
items.uk: зосередитися на боротьбі з тяжкими злочинами; взяти на приціл тяжкі злочини
items.example: With fewer officers available, the police have decided to **target serious crime** first.
more: This month's campaign **targets** drivers who don't wear seat belts.
The new police unit will **target** gangs that steal from tourists.
items.watchOut: Target тут — дієслово «зосередитися на, взяти на приціл», без прийменника: target serious crime, не target on crime. «Тяжкі злочини» — serious crime, не heavy crime.

items.pattern: street crime · noun + noun
items.meaning: crime that happens in public places, such as robbing people or snatching phones and bags
items.example: Since the police started foot patrols in the town centre, **street crime** has fallen.
more: Elderly people are often afraid of **street crime**, even in areas where it's rare.
The guidebook warns tourists about **street crime** in the old town.
items.watchOut: Crime тут зазвичай незлічуване: Street crime is falling — без артикля й без -s.

items.pattern: vehicle crime · noun + noun
items.meaning: crime involving cars and other vehicles: stealing them or stealing things from them
items.uk: злочини, пов'язані з автомобілями (крадіжки авто й з авто)
items.example: Since the new barrier and cameras went up, **vehicle crime** in the station car park has halved.
more: The police leaflet gives tips on avoiding **vehicle crime**, like parking in well-lit places.
**Vehicle crime** includes stealing cars and stealing things from them.
items.watchOut: Vehicle читається без h: /ˈviːəkl/. У розмові частіше кажуть car crime.

items.pattern: break into a house / a flat / a car · broke – broken · a break-in
items.meaning: get into a building or car by force, usually to steal something
items.example: Someone **broke into** our flat while we were on holiday and took the TV.
more: Thieves **broke into** the school kitchen and took all the chocolate biscuits.
We had a **break-in** last year, so now we've got an alarm.
items.watchOut: З додатком — break into: break into a house, не break in a house. Без додатка — break in: Someone broke in last night. Іменник — a break-in.

items.pattern: steal a car / money / sb's phone · steal – stole – stolen · have sth stolen
items.meaning: take something that belongs to someone else without permission
items.example: Someone **stole** my bike from outside the library.
more: Thieves **stole** £500 from the till while the owner was in the back room.
Our neighbours' car **was stolen** from outside their house last night.
items.watchOut: Steal — про річ: steal a car, steal money. «У мене вкрали телефон» — My phone was stolen / I had my phone stolen, не I was stolen my phone і не They robbed my phone.

items.pattern: rob sb / a bank / a shop · rob sb of sth · a robbery, a robber
items.meaning: take money or things from a person or a place, often using force or threats
items.example: Two men **robbed** a petrol station on the ring road last night.
more: Someone **robbed** my cousin as she walked home from work, but luckily she wasn't hurt.
The bank on Station Road has been **robbed** twice this year.
items.watchOut: Rob — про людину або місце: rob a tourist, rob a bank. Зазвичай не rob a car і не rob money — тут треба steal. «Його пограбували» — he was robbed; «у нього забрали гроші» — he was robbed of his money.

items.pattern: tackle / combat / fight crime (vandalism, fraud) · tackle the problem
items.meaning: take strong action to reduce crime or deal with a problem
items.uk: боротися зі злочинністю; братися за проблему
items.example: The council has hired more wardens to **tackle crime** in the town centre.
more: Every town needs more youth workers if it really wants to **tackle crime**.
Banks are working with the police to **combat** fraud.
items.watchOut: «Боротися зі злочинністю» — fight / tackle / combat crime, без with: не fight with crime. Tackle тут — братися за проблему, а не «підкат» у футболі.

items.pattern: the crime rate (goes up / comes down) · a high / low crime rate
items.meaning: how much crime there is in an area over a period of time
items.example: Estate agents say a low **crime rate** is one of the first things buyers ask about.
more: Cities with good youth clubs often have a lower **crime rate**.
The **crime rate** rose sharply after the factory closed and hundreds of people lost their jobs.
items.watchOut: «Злочинність» — crime (незлічуване), а не criminality (рідкісне слово про злочинну поведінку). «Рівень злочинності» — найчастіше the crime rate: it goes up / comes down.

items.pattern: juvenile crime · a juvenile offender · formal
items.meaning: crime committed by young people who are not yet adults
items.example: Parents and teachers met to discuss the rise in **juvenile crime** on the estate.
more: Experts say boredom is one of the main causes of **juvenile crime**.
The newspaper's article on **juvenile crime** upset many parents in the area.
items.watchOut: Вимова: /ˈdʒuːvənaɪl/, наприкінці «айл». Слово офіційне; у розмові частіше кажуть youth crime.

items.pattern: a crime wave (in a city / area)
items.meaning: a sudden increase in the amount of crime in a place
items.example: A **crime wave** in the village has left elderly residents afraid to go out after dark.
more: The local paper blamed the summer **crime wave** on a small group of teenagers.
Police say the **crime wave** is over now that they have arrested three men.

items.pattern: petty crime / theft · a petty criminal / thief
items.meaning: crime that is not very serious, such as stealing small things
items.example: Most of the problems in our area are **petty crime**: stolen bikes and the odd broken window.
more: My uncle was a **petty thief** in his youth, but he's been honest for forty years.
Tourist areas often have a lot of **petty crime**, so keep an eye on your bag.
items.watchOut: «Дрібний злочин» — petty crime (або a minor offence), не little crime. Petty /ˈpeti/ про людину означає ще «дріб'язковий».

items.pattern: the crime figures (show / come out / are published) · crime statistics
items.meaning: official numbers that show how much crime there has been
items.example: Politicians from both parties argued about what the **crime figures** really meant.
more: The **crime figures** show that bike theft has doubled in five years.
Every year the **crime figures** come out in July.
items.watchOut: «Статистика злочинності» — crime figures або crime statistics, не crime digits і не crime ciphers. Figure тут — число в статистиці.

items.pattern: a spate of burglaries / thefts / robberies / break-ins
items.meaning: a lot of similar unpleasant events, here burglaries, happening in a short time
items.example: After **a spate of burglaries** on our street, everyone fitted new locks.
more: There's been **a spate of** bike thefts outside the station this month.
The shop now closes early after **a spate of** robberies in the area.
items.watchOut: Spate — лише про неприємні події, що йдуть одна за одною: a spate of thefts, але не a spate of good news. Burglary — крадіжка зі зламом (з будинку, квартири), robbery — пограбування людини, банку, магазину.

items.pattern: vehicle theft · car theft · a vehicle theft
items.meaning: the crime of stealing cars, vans and motorbikes
items.example: Our car insurance went up because there's so much **vehicle theft** in our postcode.
more: Police have arrested a gang responsible for dozens of **vehicle thefts** across the county.
Parking in a garage at night really does reduce the risk of **vehicle theft**.
items.watchOut: «Викрадення авто» — vehicle / car theft. Hijack — захопити літак чи автобус разом із людьми, це не про звичайну крадіжку машини.

items.pattern: drug abuse · alcohol abuse
items.meaning: taking illegal drugs, or using medicines in a harmful way
items.example: A nurse came to talk to the older pupils about the dangers of **drug abuse**.
more: The charity supports families affected by **drug abuse** and **alcohol abuse**.
Long-term **drug abuse** can damage your heart and your memory.
items.watchOut: Зазвичай drug abuse — drug в однині. Abuse тут — не насильство, а шкідливе вживання, зловживання. Іменник abuse читається /əˈbjuːs/, дієслово — /əˈbjuːz/.

items.pattern: a staggering increase / rise / number / amount
items.meaning: a rise so big that it shocks or amazes you
items.example: Our gas bill showed a **staggering increase** of 70 per cent this winter.
more: The museum had a **staggering** two million visitors last year.
The new film made a **staggering** £50 million in its first weekend.
items.watchOut: Staggering — від stagger (хитатися): цифра така велика, що аж приголомшує. Іменник increase має наголос на першому складі (an INcrease), дієслово — на другому (to inCREASE).

items.pattern: mindless vandalism / violence · an act of mindless vandalism
items.meaning: damage to public or private property done for no reason at all
items.example: The council has spent thousands repairing damage caused by **mindless vandalism** in the park.
more: Breaking the swings in a children's playground is just **mindless vandalism**.
Local people cleaned up the graffiti the morning after a night of **mindless vandalism**.
items.watchOut: Vandalism незлічуване: an act of vandalism, а не a vandalism. Mindless — «бездумний, без жодної причини»; так кажуть і mindless violence.

warmup.uk: Він ніколи раніше не скоював злочину.
warmup.q: He had never ___ a crime before.
warmup.explain: Скоїти злочин — commit a crime. Make a crime — калька.

warmup.uk: У мене в метро вкрали телефон.
warmup.q: My phone was ___ on the underground.
warmup.explain: Річ вкрали — was stolen. Rob — про людину чи місце, burgle — про будинок чи квартиру.

warmup.q: A tourist was ___ near the station.
warmup.explain: Людину пограбували — was robbed. Steal — про річ, burgle — про будинок.

warmup.uk: Хтось уночі вломився в нашу машину.
warmup.explain: Вломитися кудись — break into. Break in — без додатка, break down — зламатися.

warmup.uk: Він відсидів п'ять років за пограбування.
warmup.explain: Відсидіти термін — serve (a sentence, five years). Pass a sentence — винести вирок, це робить суддя.

warmup.q: There's a lot of ___ crime around the market.

warmup.uk: Камери допомагають у боротьбі зі злочинністю.
warmup.q: Cameras help in the fight ___ crime.
warmup.explain: Боротьба зі злочинністю — the fight against crime, не with.

warmup.uk: У цьому районі високий рівень злочинності.
warmup.q: This area has a high ___ rate.
warmup.explain: Рівень злочинності — the crime rate. Злочинність — crime, а не criminality.

A.q: Burglary is a serious ___, and you can go to prison for it.
A.explain: A serious offence — тяжке правопорушення. Offender — сам правопорушник, sentence — вирок.

A.q: He was sent to prison and ___ six years of a ten-year sentence.
A.explain: Serve a sentence — відбувати покарання. Pass a sentence — винести вирок, це робить суддя.

A.q: She told the interviewer honestly that she had a criminal ___ from her teenage years.
A.explain: A criminal record — судимість. Recording — аудіо- чи відеозапис.

B.q: Two men ___ a jeweller's shop on the high street.
B.explain: Rob — про місце чи людину: rob a shop. Steal — про річ: steal rings. Вломитися — break into, з into.

B.q: The village has had a ___ of car break-ins since the summer.
B.explain: A spate of — низка неприємних подій за короткий час.

B.q: The new police chief has a clear plan to ___ crime in the suburbs.
B.explain: Tackle / combat / fight crime — боротися зі злочинністю. Struggle потребує прийменника, а commit crime — скоювати злочини.

example.title: Trouble on our street
example.uk:
Минулої весни нашу тиху вулицю сколихнула низка крадіжок зі зламом. За один тиждень злодій вломився в три будинки, а в моєї сусідки вкрали машину просто з-під її дому. Місцева газета назвала це хвилею злочинності.

На зборах мешканців поліціянтка розповіла нам, що рівень злочинності в нашому районі завжди був низьким і що здебільшого тут трапляються дрібні злочини. Вона сказала, що додаткові нічні патрулі допоможуть приборкати злочинність, а сусіди, які пильнують одне одного, дуже допомагають у боротьбі зі злочинністю.

Через місяць злодія спіймали. Виявилося, що він закоренілий злочинець із довгим списком судимостей. Тепер він відбуває покарання — чотири роки ув'язнення, — і на нашій вулиці знову спокійно.
example.en:
Last spring, a [[spate of burglaries|b14]] shook our quiet street. A burglar [[broke into|b5]] three houses in one week, and someone [[stole|b6]] my neighbour's car from her drive. The local paper called it a [[crime wave|b11]].

At a residents' meeting, a police officer told us that the [[crime rate|b9]] in our area had always been low and that most problems were [[petty crime|b12]]. She said extra night patrols would help to [[tackle crime|b8]], and that neighbours who look out for each other are a big help in [[the fight against crime|b1]].

A month later they caught the burglar. He turned out to be a [[hardened criminal|a1]] with a long [[criminal record|a9]]. Now he's [[serving a sentence|a3]] of four years, and our street is quiet again.
